# Per-second row_stroke_rate for the WORK INTERVALS of the recording that
# reported the display cue pointing the OPPOSITE WAY from the number beside it.
# Read by scripts/cue_replay.py, which scores it beside cue_work_laps.txt.
#
# A COMPANION FILE, NOT A WIDENING of cue_work_laps.txt. That file's figures are
# the ones the CUE_* comment block quotes and scripts/test_cue_replay.py pins;
# adding a third ROW to it would silently redefine "the two rows" in every
# sentence that names them. Same grammar, same absence convention, separate
# file.
#
# FORMAT
#   ROW <key> <lo> <hi> <label>     starts a row; lo/hi are the target band, spm
#   LAP <v> <v> <v> ...             one work interval, one value per second
#   Lines beginning with # and blank lines are ignored.
#
# A value of 0 is the app's NO-DATA SENTINEL, not a slow stroke: outputRate()
# returns 0.0 when nothing has been measured and drawRate renders it "--.-".
# cue_replay.py treats it as an absence, and cueBandZone maps it to CUEZ_NONE.
# 23 of the 1443 seconds here carry that zero; the other 1420 carry a reading.
#
# THE BAND IS AN ASSUMPTION, AND IT IS THE ONE WEAK LINK IN THIS FIXTURE. The
# app records no target-band setting anywhere in the file, so 16-18 below is the
# SHIPPED DEFAULT (resources/settings/properties.xml, targetLo 16 / targetHi 18)
# and not a decoded value. Every figure derived from this row is therefore
# conditional on the athlete having rowed the default band. The reported "blue
# at 20 spm" symptom does NOT reproduce at 16-18 -- zero seconds of it -- and
# nothing in this file can settle whether that is because the band was different
# or because the symptom was misremembered. It is left unresolved rather than
# explained away.
#
# PROVENANCE, so this is reproducible from the original with any FIT decoder:
#   source file    i183553852.fit, recorded 2026-09-05 on app v0.9
#   values         the 'row_stroke_rate' DEVELOPER FIELD (id 0) of record
#                  messages (FIT global message 20), in timestamp order
#   work seconds   record messages whose 'step_type' DEVELOPER FIELD (id 17)
#                  is 2 == SFIT_WORK, split into maximal CONTIGUOUS RUNS
#                  -> 8 runs, 1443 seconds, one run per interval_num 1..8
#   why not laps   cue_work_laps.txt cuts on lap messages because its two
#                  recordings predate the step_type field. This one has it, and
#                  it is the better boundary: it selects the seconds the app was
#                  actually IN a work step, which is the question the cue is
#                  being asked. Cutting instead on lap messages (global 19,
#                  start_time inclusive to timestamp exclusive, lap_step_type
#                  == 2) gives 8 laps and 1440 seconds -- three fewer, at the
#                  interval boundaries. Both are recorded so a reader who
#                  reproduces 1440 knows which convention they used.
#   precision      float32 in the file, written here to 4 decimal places with
#                  trailing zeros stripped. That is exact for both band edges
#                  (16, 18) and 1e-4 spm elsewhere, which cannot move a zone
#                  decision.
#
# CROSS-CHECKS a reader can run against the original in two minutes, all pinned
# by scripts/test_cue_replay.py:
#   seconds per interval     181, 180, 181, 180, 181, 180, 180, 180
#   interval medians         17.6, 18.3, 17.6, 17.9, 18.7, 22.7, 23.8, 23.4
#   no-data seconds/interval 0, 0, 5, 2, 0, 5, 11, 0
#   row median               19.48 spm over the 1420 readings
#   fastest / slowest        38.5 spm / 6.0 spm
#
# NOTHING BUT STROKE RATE IS HERE. No timestamps, no position, no cadence -- the
# file carries only what the cue's decision function consumes. The native
# cadence, speed and rate_base series that the START-baseline defect is argued
# from are NOT here and must not be added: this file is consumed positionally
# and every cue figure would then depend on a series the cue never sees.
ROW reversal 16 18 8x3' progressive, i183553852
